title: The operator picks one of three UI outcomes and the manifest records the choice
iWant: an explicit choice about whether we get an operator-facing Secrets page and where it lives
soThat: the project ends up with the UI it needs and nothing it does not

acceptanceCriteria.description: At apply the working agent records the operator's UI choice as one of `integrate`, `admin-spa`, or `none` on the manifest header field `uiIntegration.mode`.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a fresh apply of the blueprint against a project with no `secrets.yaml`
acceptanceCriteria.when: the working agent elicits the choice and writes the manifest
acceptanceCriteria.then: the manifest's `uiIntegration.mode` string equals one of `integrate`, `admin-spa`, or `none` and no other value passes manifest validation

acceptanceCriteria.description: When mode is `integrate`, the deployed admin UI exposes a Secrets page whose surface matches TAC-905: a list keyed by name showing environment, owner, `lastRotatedAt`, and `rotationDays`; no cell on the page renders a secret value.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project with `uiIntegration.mode: 'integrate'` that has realised TAC-905
acceptanceCriteria.when: the operator fetches the deployed Secrets page and inspects its rendered content
acceptanceCriteria.then: every row carries the fields above and byte-equality checks against the vendor-resolved secret values return no match anywhere on the rendered page

acceptanceCriteria.description: When mode is `none`, no Secrets page is exposed anywhere in the deployed application; the CLI plus audit sink are the only operator surfaces the blueprint contributes.
acceptanceCriteria.when: the deployed application is scanned for a Secrets page under any admin path
acceptanceCriteria.then: no path returns a page whose contents identify as the Secrets Management surface (no page metadata declaring it, no HTML fragment matching the TAC-905 shape)
